assumptions: No tolerance was given for frequency, so a default of tol_pct: 2 is used.
No tolerance was given for duty cycle, so a default of tol_abs: 1 percentage point is used.
A 500 ms measurement window is used, giving ~500 periods of the 1 kHz signal for a stable frequency/duty measurement.
Requirement 2 (signal starts on its own after reset) is verified implicitly by measuring the waveform right after the mandatory 1000 ms boot wait, with no stimulus step preceding it.

checks.requirement: The signal on D5 has a frequency of 1 kHz and a duty cycle of 25%, starting on its own right after reset.
checks.reason: nothing was measured for 'frequency_hz' (null, e.g. no signal or no response); expected ≈ 1000 Hz ± 2%
checks.feedback: No signal is seen because the PWM sequence that was actually configured (SEQ[0]) is never started. In pwm_start() the code calls NRF_PWM0->TASKS_SEQSTART[1] = 1, which starts sequence 1, but only SEQ[0] was set up with PTR/CNT/etc. Since SEQ[1] registers are left at their reset (zero) values, the peripheral has no valid duty data to play and produces no toggling output on D5.

checks.requirement: The signal on D5 has a frequency of 1 kHz and a duty cycle of 25%, starting on its own right after reset.
checks.reason: nothing was measured for 'duty_pct' (null, e.g. no signal or no response); expected ≈ 25% ± 1 pt
checks.feedback: Duty cycle can't be measured because, as with the frequency check, the wrong sequence index is triggered in pwm_start(): TASKS_SEQSTART[1] instead of TASKS_SEQSTART[0]. The configured duty_seq array (250 | 0x8000) is referenced by SEQ[0], but that sequence is never started, so no PWM waveform with any duty cycle is ever produced on D5.

checks.requirement: The signal on D5 has a frequency of 1 kHz and a duty cycle of 25%, starting on its own right after reset.
checks.feedback: Zero edges were measured, consistent with the PWM never actually starting. The fix should start in the same place: NRF_PWM0->TASKS_SEQSTART[1] in pwm_start() starts the unconfigured sequence 1 rather than the configured sequence 0 (SEQ[0]). Check that this is changed to TASKS_SEQSTART[0] so the configured duty_seq data is actually played out on D5.

checks.requirement: Must use a hardware timer/PWM peripheral (not analogWrite() or delay()-based bit-banging).
checks.reason: Not electrically observable: a correctly timed 1 kHz/25% waveform can be produced by either a hardware timer or careful software timing; this can only be checked by TA code review.

checks.requirement: Register values/constants are commented and their computation explained.
checks.reason: Code documentation/comments cannot be verified electrically; requires manual review of the submitted source.
